q0363: Detect intruders already inside = honeypots (any contact is suspicious) and DNS sinkholes (reveal hosts calling known-bad domains).
q0364: Detect tampering with released software = hashing: publish the hash so anyone can check the file. Code signing adds proof of who published it.
q0365: Adding a new cloud app to existing enterprise SSO = configure a SAML federation trust.
q0366: Public Wi-Fi + an ignored certificate warning = on-path (man-in-the-middle) attack.
q0367: Redundant equipment behind a single ISP link = a single point of failure.
q0368: Segmenting an unpatchable system: category = technical, type = compensating.
q0369: The attacker can already log in to the stolen device → remote wipe. FDE no longer helps once someone is logged in.
q0370: Risk left after controls = residual. Risk before any controls = inherent.
q0371: Make reverse engineering harder = code obfuscation.
q0372: MFA factors: something you know, have or are. Somewhere you are and something you do are attributes.
q0373: Guessable passwords → longer minimum length and a bigger character set (length matters most). Better hashing protects stored hashes, not guessability.
q0374: Inbound connections on an odd port right after installing untrusted software = a backdoor listening for the attacker.
q0375: Elastic memory, scalable storage and circuit resilience without buying hardware = IaaS.
q0376: DNS sinkhole = answer lookups for known-bad domains with a safe address, blocking the connection and logging the infected host.
q0377: GPS coordinates, camera model and timestamps inside a photo = metadata (EXIF).
q0378: Digitally signing email (S/MIME) = non-repudiation and integrity. Encrypting it = confidentiality.
q0379: IoT cryptography: the first consideration is resource constraints (CPU, memory, battery), which is why lightweight algorithms exist.
q0380: Guest Wi-Fi that asks for a code, a receipt number or acceptance of terms = captive portal.
q0381: The most volatile evidence is CPU registers, cache and RAM. Capture memory before powering off.
q0382: Proof that controls operated effectively over a period (six to twelve months) = SOC 2 Type 2. Type 1 = design at a single point in time.
q0383: Data center destroyed → execute the DRP right away to restore IT for essential services. The BCP is the broader umbrella.
q0384: Separation of duties = preventive. Audits, log correlation and alerts are detective.
q0385: Servers up internally but unreachable from elsewhere, with huge inbound traffic = DoS.
q0386: One common element across a phishing wave (the URL shortener) → block it at the proxy. Subject lines change every time.
q0388: Keep only what is required, then destroy it = retention policy (with a disposal schedule).
q0389: Credentials committed to code repositories = the common accidental cloud leak.
q0390: Classification lets security requirements attach to each level: encrypt, restrict and retain by label.
q0391: Scanning with no account = non-credentialed scan (the outsider's view). Credentialed scans see far more, such as missing patches.
q0392: Real-world adversary tactics and techniques, mapped to mitigations = MITRE ATT&CK.
